title: M/s Threads India Limited v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Arvind Kumar Tripathi and Salil Kumar Rai, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed following Dev Prayag; additional security demand not bad.
headnote: A consumer’s writ to quash an additional-security bill under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and to strike down clause 4.20(i)(L) as ultra vires ss. 47(4) and 47(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003, was dismissed. A coordinate Bench in Dev Prayag Paper Mill had already held that demand of additional security by the distribution licensee is not bad; this petition failed for those reasons.
facts: M/s Threads India Limited challenged Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.’s bill dated 21 February 2014 for Rs.54,74,938 as additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. It also sought interest on and refund of security already deposited, and declarations that amended clause 4.20(i)(L) was ultra vires sections 47(4) and 47(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003 and retrospective from 10 June 2003. An earlier Division Bench had stayed the demand on 12 March 2014.

holding_units.holding: The writ seeking to quash an additional-security demand under clause 4.20, and to declare clause 4.20(i)(L) of the 14.9.2006 amendment ultra vires ss. 47(4) and 47(5) of the Electricity Act, 2003 (and retrospective from 10.6.2003), is dismissed. Following Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Writ-C No. 30898 of 2016, 21.3.2017), demand of additional security by the distribution licensee is not bad.
holding_units.flag: petition pleaded cl. 4.20(i)(L) and cl. 4.20(i) of the 2006 amendment; Court did not separately parse those sub-clauses
